recon.notes: Parser config at recon: name "Dallas Eagle", urls ["https://www.thedallaseagle.com/events/"], no urlDiscoveryDepth / discovery patterns / alwaysBear / siteRole / automationEnabled / calendarLookaheadMonths overrides (defaults apply: MEC lookahead 2 months; global allowPastEvents true, daysToLookAhead null); metadata website/facebook/instagram/mastodon. Platform confirmed by working endpoints: WordPress REST /wp-json/wp/v2/mec-events (X-WP-Total 290) and the MEC admin-ajax month feed. Site clock at fetch: today "20260909" (fetched 2026-09-10 01:43 UTC). Every occurrence on this site is its own WordPress post with its own slug — there is no ?occurrence= parameter and no Event JSON-LD anywhere (page JSON-LD @graph is Organization/WebSite/BreadcrumbList/Person/WebPage/Article only); dates come from the grid cell (data-mec-cell) and the page Date block, times from the page Time block / grid tooltip. Event pages carry no flyer images (only the venue logo), so there is no flyer rung. Recon done read-only with curl; no browser rung was needed. Note for anyone replaying the feed: a malformed POST (mec_year with a space, empty mec_month) makes the site answer HTTP 500 "There has been a critical error on this website." — that is the request, not the calendar.

coverage.basis: Primary door: the MEC month-feed POST replayed for Sep, Oct, Nov, Dec 2026 (30/44/54/43 grid cells; 171 cells → 153 distinct date+post pairs after removing the neighbouring-month spill-over cells each grid repeats; 27/40/44/42 posts by month). The static /events/ page renders the identical September grid (30 cells). All 153 linked posts were fetched; every page Date block matches its grid cell and every page title matches its grid title. Second door: WP REST mec-events (X-WP-Total 290) contains all 153 slugs plus 137 posts whose WordPress publish dates are all 2024–2025 (old occurrences, i.e. past listings — counted, not enumerated); no 2026-created post exists outside the four grids, so nothing is published past Dec 31 2026. Third door, the mec-events sitemap, is stale (only 4 of 153 live slugs) and was discarded. The January 2027 feed carries only December spill-over cells (zero January-dated posts) and February 2027 is a bare grid, while August 2026 is also empty, so the published horizon is exactly Sep 8–Dec 31 2026 and coverage.occurrenceWindow is set to Sep 9–Dec 31 (114 days) instead of recon+90 so that every dated post the site publishes is recorded. Of the 152 in-window posts, 85 belong to 11 series whose repeat rule the site states in the post body (each dated post listed as an origin:"listed" occurrence with page evidence) and 67 are singles — several titles recur monthly (Gear Night ×9, Sweet Tea ×5, Drink Draw and Dine ×4, Pet Night ×4, Femme, Throb, Ignite, 80s Retro ×3 …) but state no rule and are kept as singles per the no-inferred-recurrence rule. The one remaining post (Sep 8 Motley Clue Trivia, Expired) is the only past listing on the grids. publishedEventCount = 11 series + 67 singles = 78.
knownGaps: No flyer images are published on event pages (only the venue logo), so nothing was read from images; three Ignite posts and the Sep 24 Latino Night post have no body text at all — title, date and time are the entire published record.
Months were read only through 2027-02; a post dated March 2027 or later would be missed here, though the REST cross-check (no 2026-created post is absent from the Sep–Dec grids) makes that unlikely.

traps.label: Motley Clue Trivia — Sep 8 cell on the September grid with an "Expired" label
traps.why: The configured page renders the whole current month, so the one Tuesday already gone (Sep 8, 8–10pm) sits on it flagged Expired. It is a real past occurrence of the Motley Clue Trivia series, not a future event. Global config.allowPastEvents is true, so extracting it is correct behaviour, not a bug.
traps.note: Post: https://www.thedallaseagle.com/events/motley-clue-trivia-22/ (Date "Sep 08 2026"). Counted, not enumerated: it is the only expired cell on any fetched grid.

traps.label: "End at: September 10, 2026 - 2:00 am" tooltip/list line under every overnight event
traps.why: Overnight events render two dated lines — "Start from: <date> - 9:00 pm" then "End at: <next day> - 2:00 am". The End at line names a different calendar day and looks like a second listing; it is the end of the same event, never a start and never a second occurrence.
traps.note: Config comment says #1540 end-marker gate covers this. 2026-09-10 02:00 must not appear as a start date.

traps.label: "August" / "October" month navigator links above the grid
traps.why: The previous/next month controls (data-mec-month="08"/"10") are AJAX navigator buttons, not events. Following them as links yields the same /events/ URL; the real month change is the admin-ajax form POST.

openQuestions.q: Why did run 20260909-072307 yield 1 kept + 6 bear-dropped events from a page that links 30 dated posts (plus 84 more via the two default lookahead months)? The static page and the month feed both list every post plainly; the drop appears to be crawl/extraction-side, not site-side.

Slug/title drift: several posts reuse an older slug for a differently titled event (bear-night-2 = LatinX Encuerados, frequency-featuring-george-flores-4 = Latino Night, 80s-retro-4 = Rewind, gear-night-20/blacklite-3/gear-night-21 = SHOCK Therapy, latinx-encuerados-3/4/6 = Ignite, swell-* = SWPOL, trash-disco-with-dj-blaine-4 = Trash Disco with DJ Apthout). Any title derived from the URL slug will be wrong for these; the h1 / grid title is the truth.

Run 20260909-072307 recorded the Oct 9 Bear Night post as title "Second Fridays" (the body's opening phrase) with FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=2FR — a title-extraction miss on a page whose h1 and grid label both read "Bear Night".

Should calendarLookaheadMonths be raised to 3 for this parser? December (42 posts) is published now but sits beyond the default 2-month feed replay, so 22 December-only entries here carry expect.extracted "unknown".
